brief.title: Midterm brief: Sunday, October 25
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Sunday, October 25

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats, from Inside Elections' 212 D / 205 R to The Economist's and Silver Bulletin's 230 D ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 10 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 91.5% for the House and 66.5% for the Senate, the Senate down one point ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 25.

## What moved
- **Forecaster updates (Oct 24):** 19 House rating changes, 14 toward Democrats and 5 toward Republicans ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Economist made 11 (7 toward Democrats), including PA-01, TX-35 and CO-04 to Tossup and MN-01 and NV-02 to Lean R; Split Ticket made 7, including FL-07 and FL-22 to Tossup.
- **House consensus:** NC-01 moved from Tossup to Lean D. No race entered or left the tracked list (62 races).
- **Senate:** No rating changes, and no poll average moved past the thresholds.

## Races to watch today
- **Pennsylvania House:** New polls find Democrats ahead in four key Pennsylvania House races ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/us/politics/polls-pennsylvania-house-midterms-battlegrounds.html)). They are not in the averages yet.
- **Alaska Senate (Tossup):** Democrats asked a judge to dismiss the administration's challenge to the race ([NBC News via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixwFBVV95cUxNcFRtY2d0ODhsOVMxck1mTTNfQVZYQWpRWUw4cDlGOHdfOERLSXdscmdVYlVRaERsM1RXWGNUeUFsMjlYRlY3a1RDNEF6cDRBeUZUWm1TcjRFYTk4cXY2UWd3T0hxM3VGdTZvZllEUDNFSF8yU3psdUhPWDBWOFdCTDlZX3NNcWNnc1EwMFhHZmFsc2hyeFlxYUtDcHR1LTZkZGkzb0R5MXpGZGNLYko0eTVPM2l2aVNrcV9vREhHelFsRHI0bW00?oc=5)). Average: D+0.8.
- **Kansas Senate (Tossup):** The NYT profiles Marshall, a Trump loyalist, fighting to hold a seat in a deep-red state ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/us/politics/roger-marshall-kansas-senate.html)). Average: D+0.5.
- **Maine Senate (Tossup):** NBC News reports how women break could decide the race; Collins won them in 2020 ([NBC News via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxNOThyajVBVnpMSklwVm9nREo1YlpLdWZTUUltTTZEeV9oNHhINDZwd1lmTTZZbENpb3p0UVFBdExwYlB3OGJFNzNad0k0WFQtYnRPbV9KVG9sdHp0QUhZTEVtdlJTeW9mUzJ6YVZYRVhQYjVHTXN6NkdNcWZNeUxmUmVyY1Y4bjVaZlpMWWdUZXhYOTJUWTNnQ0c3d1BpaGtnVTZlWnU0N25TMmF2bTJYN0hVX2toNE85T3RuOVltVQ?oc=5)). Average: D+2.2.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 23, 1,453,516 ballots were cast, 136% of the 2022 total at the same point (1,067,593) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-24%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 24 the total reached 1,544,674 at D 41.5% / R 23.8% / other 34.7% ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Large states (Oct 24):** Florida has 2,597,716 ballots (1,220,521 in person) at D 39.8% / R 39.7%, against registration of D 30.1% / R 41.5%; California 2,943,863 at D 47.0% / R 27.1% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from secretary of state data).
- **Senate battlegrounds:** Arizona 861,138 at D 38.4% / R 38.7% (Oct 24, via a private compiler); Iowa 207,774 at D 50.9% / R 32.0% and Nebraska 136,433 at D 41.4% / R 42.0% (Oct 23) ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/)).

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** Pod Save America's new episode features Eric Holder on "stopping the steal"; the feed gives only the title ([Pod Save America](https://audioboom.com/posts/8968588)).
- **Center:** GD Politics posted a poll hunter's guide to the final stretch ([GD Politics](https://www.gdpolitics.com/p/bonus-a-poll-hunters-guide-to-the-4e1)).
- **Center-right:** The WSJ reports MAHA support for Republicans isn't guaranteed this year ([WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/the-maha-maga-alliance-is-fracturing-before-the-midterms-27b9bcf7?mod=rss_socialpoliticsfeed)).
- **Right:** National Review argues a Washington Post fact-check defended El-Sayed ([National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/10/the-washington-post-parodies-the-fact-check-genre-in-el-sayeds-defense/)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- The generic ballot averages D+7.2 across 4 polls, unchanged; Pew has D+8, ending Oct 4 ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms)).
- The NYT reports Latinos are now America's most important swing voters ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/us/politics/latino-voters-poll-midterm-elections.html)).

## Coverage note
All 24 sources reported, and early vote covered 27 states; Pennsylvania, Iowa, Maine and Nebraska are from Oct 23. California's party shares dropped about three points in a day while 6% of ballots shifted out of the D/R/other split, so treat them with caution. Kalshi had no priced markets. Candidate parties remain unresolved for seven House races (FL-22, NV-02, NY-21, NC-11, SC-01, TX-23, TX-35).
